heading: Give the box the arrow.

04 / 15 01 / A parent state
Give the box the arrow.

Put the four working states inside on. A POWER_OFF arrow from on applies to any active child. One arrow replaces four copies.

A parent is active when its child is active. Events try the inner state first, then its parent. Here no child handles POWER_OFF.

heading: Regions can live inside a parent.

Regions can live inside a parent.

Put the player’s two regions inside on, beside off. POWER_OFF now leaves both regions. POWER_ON starts them again at stopped and audible.

Hierarchy removes repeated exits. Regions remove repeated combinations. You can use both in one chart.

heading: Less repetition. Same machine.
text:
15 / 15 Take it with you
Less repetition. Same machine.

A statechart is a state machine whose states can contain other states, active one at a time or several at once.

Two signs in a flat machine tell you where those extra structures may help.

What to look for
Two useful signs
1 / REPEATED DESTINATION

One event leaves many states for the same place → try a parent.

2 / INDEPENDENT WORDS

State names combine independent choices → try regions.

Flatten either structure and the behaviour remains an ordinary state machine.
Scope & correctness notes
